reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) supports using displacement covariances for vibrational entropy in elemental solids and mentions extension to a HEA, but it does not address fluid phases, configurational entropy, or the claimed speed-up and accuracy relative to TOR-TILD or full AIMD free-energy workflows.
premises: Vibrational entropy can be computed from the covariance matrix of atomic displacements via a Gaussian approximation.
Short AIMD or Monte Carlo trajectories suffice to capture the displacement covariances needed for entropy.
The method works for solids and can be extended to fluids and multicomponent alloys.
The approach yields free-energy accuracy comparable to full AIMD (within ~10%) with an order-of-magnitude speed-up.
The method is valid under moderate anharmonicity where the Gaussian approximation holds.
